document.title: IIR Taliban Leadership, Part 1 – Mullah Omar and the Council of Ministers
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Updated biographical summaries of Taliban members. Notes one of Omar's sons was reportedly killed in October 2001 air strikes, Mullah Hassan Akhund's rise to Vice President of the Council of Ministers, and Rabbani's death from cancer in April 2001. Excised.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Founded by Mullah Omar in 1994 according to the report; governs through a Council of Ministers.

organizations.name: Council of Ministers
organizations.notes: Taliban cabinet; Vice President Hassan Akhund. Met several times at Turabi's house.

organizations.name: Hezb-i-Islami (Khalis)
organizations.notes: Anti-Soviet mujahideen party in which Omar, Hassan Akhund and Khaksar served.

organizations.name: Harakat-i-Inqilab-i-Islami (Mohammadi)
organizations.notes: Anti-Soviet mujahideen party of Mohammadi; Abbas and Turabi fought with it.

organizations.name: Ittehad-i-Islami (Sayyaf)
organizations.notes: Sayyaf's mujahideen party; Obaidullah, Abbas and Turabi fought with it.

organizations.name: Harakat-i-Tulaba-i-Islam
organizations.notes: Student wing of Harakat-i-Inqilab-i-Islami (Mohammadi) in southwestern Afghanistan, led by Muttawakil in the Soviet era.

organizations.name: Darul Uloom Haqqania
organizations.notes: Madrassah at Akora Khattak, NWFP, where Kabir graduated.

organizations.name: Haqqani madrassahs in Miranshah
organizations.notes: Where Kabir taught before the Taliban emerged.

organizations.name: UNSMA
organizations.notes: Its Kabul office was confiscated in June 2001 and Muttawakil negotiated with it.

organizations.name: Ministry of National Defense
organizations.notes: Led by Obaidullah; supervised by Hassan Akhund.

organizations.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
organizations.notes: Led by Muttawakil, with deputies Jalil and Zahid.

organizations.name: Ministry of Interior
organizations.notes: Led by Abdul Razaq; Khaksar is deputy for security.

organizations.name: Ahmadia, Noorul Madris and Ashafia madrasas
organizations.notes: Quetta religious schools where Muttawakil studied.

organizations.name: Khalqi communist party
organizations.notes: Muttawakil's family and uncle Khadam were affiliated; former Khalqis were brought into the Taliban armed forces.

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Not named in the text; linked only through bin Ladin's family tie to Omar.

events.description: Communist coup; Omar joins the mujahideen. Muttawakil's father is killed by the Taraki regime.
Abbas Akhund seeks refuge in Quetta.
Kabir leaves for Pakistan to study at madrassahs.
Khost falls to the mujahideen; Kabir is wounded.
Omar founds the Taliban in Kandahar.
Fall of Kabul to the Taliban. Khaksar appointed deputy interior minister for security affairs; Kabir becomes governor of Nangarhar and Governor-General of the Eastern Zone.
Ashgabat peace talks; Muttawakil negotiated privately without permission and lost clout.
Hassan Akhund sanctions destruction of the Bamiyan Buddhas as a religious duty.
Hassan Akhund confiscates the UNSMA office in Kabul after a lease dispute.
One of Omar's sons is reportedly killed in air strikes.
DIA information report on Taliban leadership, Part 1, is issued.
Mullah Khaksar Akhund appointed Deputy Minister of Interior for Security Affairs after serving as intelligence chief.
Mullah Mohammad Abbas Akhund sought refuge in Quetta.
Mullah Obaidullah prepared the demolition plan for destruction of the Buddhas and house burnings in Bamiyan.
Mullah Omar born in Noori village near Kandahar.
Following the communist coup, Omar joined the mujahideen movement.
Omar founded the Taliban in Kandahar region.
One of Omar's sons reportedly killed in October 2001 air strikes.
Hassan Akhund sanctioned destruction of the Bamiyan Buddhas, calling it a religious duty.
Hassan Akhund confiscated the UNSMA office in Kabul after a lease dispute.
Kabir left for Pakistan to pursue religious education.
Kabir wounded when Khost fell to the mujahideen.
After the fall of Kabul, Kabir appointed Governor of Nangarhar and Governor-General of Eastern Zone.
Maulawi Abdul Ghaffar killed by Taraki's communist regime.
Ashgabat peace talks; Muttawakil conducted private negotiations without permission.
Khaksar Akhund appointed Deputy Minister of Interior for Security Affairs.
Abbas Akhund sought refuge in Quetta.

key_claims: Mullah Omar, a Hotak Pashtun from Uruzgan and Kandahar, founded the Taliban in 1994 after fighting under Nek Mohammad of Hezb-i-Islami (Khalis).
Omar is reported to be bin Ladin's son-in-law and to have lost a son in the October 2001 air strikes.
Vice President Hassan Akhund supervises the defense, intelligence, interior, justice and other key ministries and is a hardliner.
Maulawi Abdul Kabir, Jalaluddin Haqqani's former commander, controls the Eastern Zone smuggling nexus and launders money, while keeping Pakistani contacts.
Many Taliban ministers, including Obaidullah, Abbas and Turabi, came from Hezb-i-Islami (Khalis), Harakat-i-Inqilab or Ittehad-i-Islami during the anti-Soviet jihad.
Obaidullah planned the Bamiyan Buddha demolition and rivals Kabir; Muttawakil was distrusted after the private Ashgabat negotiations.
